canonical_question: Why is the BCC precipitate composition reported as 'Fe-Co rich' when it contains 49 at% Fe and 40 at% Co, and how does this partitioning differ from the matrix?

question_variants.question: Why is the BCC precipitate composition reported as 'Fe-Co rich' when it contains 49 at% Fe and 40 at% Co, and how does this partitioning differ from the matrix?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper provides the specific average compositions for both the BCC phase (6Al-40Co-49Fe-5Ni) and the B2 phase (32Al-18Co-17Fe-33Ni). The BCC phase is described as 'Fe-Co rich' because it contains significantly higher Fe (49%) and Co (40%) compared to the B2 matrix (17% Fe, 18% Co), while the matrix is Al/Ni rich.

answers.answer: The average composition of the BCC phase is 6Al-40Co-49Fe-5Ni (at%), while the B2 phase is 32Al-18Co-17Fe-33Ni (at%). The BCC phase is Fe-Co rich due to its high Fe (49%) and Co (40%) content compared to the B2 phase which is Al (32%) and Ni (33%) rich.
answers.measurement_outcome: Average compositions of BCC and B2 phases
answers.mechanism: Elemental partitioning between B2 and BCC phases
evidence_spans: The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy.
The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions.
